extracted.intended_audience: corporate finance and legal teams, SEC reporting specialists, auditors and accountants preparing registration statements and merger proxy statements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and interpretive rules for the financial statement, audit, updating, pro forma and disclosure requirements when preparing Forms S-4, F-4, N-14 and related merger proxy/registration filings under Regulation S‑X and S‑K.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-06 accommodation (9- to 12‑month period may satisfy a full fiscal year)
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-06 permits financial statements for a period of 9 to 12 months to satisfy the requirements for a full fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The accommodation applies to audits of historical financial statements. The period selected needs to be audited and should immediately follow or precede the other (full) fiscal year for which audited financial statements are provided (i.e., there should not be a gap between audited periods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on applying Rule 3-06 when multiple fiscal years required
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than one fiscal year is required under Rule 3-05, registrants may rely on S-X Rule 3-06 for only one of the required fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, if acquisition significance requires two years of financials and the acquisition is >40%, registrants may provide a 9- to 12-month audited period for one of the two required years, but the audited financial statements for the second period must cover a full fiscal year. Registrants may choose which fiscal year to satisfy with the 9- to 12-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of interim audited period may require unaudited interim information
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice of a 9- to 12-month audited period may result in a need to provide unaudited interim financial information (e.g., if audited as of September 30, may need to provide unaudited interim for subsequent period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show different combinations of audited and unaudited periods that can satisfy Rule 3-05 depending on filing date and acquisition date; registrants should plan sets of audited/unaudited statements accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contiguity requirement for audited periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The 9- to 12-month audited period selected under Rule 3-06 should immediately follow or precede the other (full) fiscal year for which audited financial statements are provided; there should not be a gap between audited periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants have the option to determine which fiscal year period will be satisfied by providing 9 to 12 months of audited financial statements, but the period selected needs to be audited and contiguous with the other audited year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating pre-acquisition financial statements when Rule 3-06 applied
rubrics_metrics.description: If audited financial statements for a 9- to 12-month period were used under Rule 3-06 and those statements are included in a subsequently filed registration statement, proxy statement, or Form 8-K that requires updated financials, the audited financial statements for the full 12 months will be required to comply with updating rules (S-X Rule 3-12 or 8-08).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not acceptable to provide unaudited interim financial statements for the subsequent three-month period (i.e., the fourth quarter) to satisfy the updating requirement. Example: if a registrant filed with nine-month audited period in a Form 8-K and later files a registration effective more than 89 days after the target’s year-end, audited 12-month statements are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of applying or not applying Rule 3-06 on required updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Rule 3-06 was applied initially affects what must be filed in a Form 8-K and what updates are required when later filing a registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Rule 3-06 was applied (audited nine-month period used), the registrant will need to update to audited 12 months when filing a registration statement beyond the age thresholds; if Rule 3-06 was not applied, previously filed audited full years plus any unaudited interim periods were filed and the registration filing still requires the audited annual statements for the newest year (no additional unaudited interim statements would be required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Rule 3-06 for unaudited pro forma financial information
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-06 may be applied to unaudited pro forma financial information only in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 9- to 12-month period for unaudited pro forma is permitted only when the registrant’s financial statements for its most recent fiscal year are for a period of 9 to 12 months (i.e., the registrant applies the Rule 3-06 accommodation). If the registrant’s most recent fiscal year is 12 months, a full 12-month period of operations for the acquired entity (that is within 93 days of the registrant’s year-end) must be included in the pro forma financial information.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use Forms S-4, F-4 and N-14
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms S-4, F-4 and N-14 are registration statements used when the legal acquirer registers securities that will be used as consideration in a merger or acquisition; Form F-4 applies to foreign private issuers, Form N-14 to investment companies/BDCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms generally require all financial statements under Reg S‑X, including Rule 3-05 financial statements for acquired businesses and pro forma financial information under Article 11. The registration statement often incorporates proxy solicitation materials (wraparound Form S-4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wraparound Form S-4 and age/update implications
rubrics_metrics.description: A wraparound Form S-4 combines a registration statement with proxy materials (the Form S-4 cover wrapped around proxy materials); the required age of financial statements in a wraparound is determined by the effective date of the Form S-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Form S-4 becomes effective before the proxy is mailed, if mailing the proxy is delayed more than a few days after effectiveness, updating the financial statements in the proxy may be required based on the mailing date. See Form 8-K considerations when financial statements were previously filed on a Form S-4 registration statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form F-4 specific age/currentness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements filed on a Form F-4 must remain current in a merger or acquisition transaction until shareholder approval has occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants filing a Form F-4 may have to update the financial statements after the filing to comply with the age requirements applicable to F-4. See additional guidance for acquired foreign businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roll-up transaction additional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Roll-up transactions require special attention in a Form S-4 registration statement and additional disclosure and pro forma requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General Instruction I of Form S-4 and General Instruction G of Form F-4 require compliance with Subpart 229.900 of Reg S-K in addition to Form S-4 disclosure requirements. See Reg S-K Item 914 (Pro forma financial statements: selected financial data) for additional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form S-4 Item 14/registrant disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 14 (Information With Respect To Registrants Other Than S-3 Registrants) requires furnishing various disclosures such as Item 101 (description of business), Item 102 (description of property), Item 103 (legal proceedings), Item 201 (market price/dividends), and financial statements meeting Regulation S-X including Rule 3-05 and Article 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires Item 302, Item 303 (MD&A), Item 304 (changes/disagreements with accountants), Item 305 (market risk), and schedules required by Regulation S-X. Schedules required by Reg S-X shall be filed as 'Financial Statement Schedules' pursuant to Item 21. The Form lists specific items to furnish in lieu of other items when registrant does not qualify to use Form S-3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form S-4 Item 17/target company disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 17 prescribes information to be furnished about the company being acquired: if subject to Exchange Act reporting, furnish information required by Item 14; if not, furnish a brief description of business plus specified items (e.g., Item 201, Item 303, Item 304(b)) and financial statements when significance thresholds are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the company being acquired is significant to the registrant in excess of the 20% level (per §210.3-05(b)(2)), provide financial statements of the company being acquired for the latest fiscal year in conformity with GAAP, and prior years if previously provided to its security holders. If significance is at or below the 20% level, no financial information (including pro forma and comparative per share information) for the company being acquired need be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance tests and thresholds (20% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether financial statements of the company being acquired must be provided, apply the significance tests in Rule 1-02(w); generally, if the acquired company is significant in excess of the 20% level, provide latest fiscal year GAAP financials; if at or below 20%, no financial information is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The instructions state the method for determining significance and reference Rule 1-02(w) for the specific tests. Provide prior fiscal years' statements only if the target provided them to its security holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit practicability and prior-year audit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial statements required for the latest fiscal year need be audited only to the extent practicable; fiscal years before the latest need not be audited if they were not previously audited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This instruction recognizes practical constraints on auditing historical periods but requires auditing where practicable and as otherwise required (e.g., when used for resales by deemed underwriters per Rule 3-05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-U.S. GAAP financial statements – reconciliation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If financial statements are prepared on the basis of a comprehensive body of accounting principles other than U.S. GAAP, provide a reconciliation to U.S. GAAP in accordance with Item 17 of Form 20-F unless a reconciliation is unavailable or not obtainable without unreasonable cost or expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a minimum, provide a narrative description of all material variations in accounting principles, practices and methods used in preparing the non-U.S. GAAP financial statements from those accepted in the U.S. when reconciliation is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resales by deemed underwriters require audited statements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Form is used to register resales to the public by any person who is deemed an underwriter with respect to the securities being reoffered, the financial statements must be audited for the fiscal years required to be presented under paragraph (b)(2) of Rule 3-05 of Regulation S-X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This imposes stricter audit requirements where the registration is being used for public resale by a deemed underwriter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly financial and Form 10-Q equivalence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 17 requires quarterly financial and other information as would have been required had the company being acquired been required to file Part I of Form 10-Q for the most recent quarter for which such a report would have been on file at the time the registration statement becomes effective or for a period ending as of a more recent date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires schedules under Rules 12-15, 28 and 29 of Regulation S-X. This ensures recent interim reporting for the target to align with what investors would expect from an SEC reporting company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target entity determination is based on legal form of transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The entity considered the 'target' for purposes of Form S-4 financial statement requirements is determined based on the legal form of the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, in a reverse acquisition between two operating entities, the target entity’s financial statements for the purposes of Form S-4 are those of the legal target, which may be the accounting acquirer. Reference: SEC staff guidance (FRM 2200.1).
